question: What directional relationship do yellow center line markings and white lane line markings communicate?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Yellow center line markings communicate that traffic on either side of the line is traveling in opposite directions, while white lane line markings communicate that traffic on either side of the line is traveling in the same direction. In short, yellow separates opposing traffic flows and white separates same-direction traffic flows, with the pattern (broken vs. solid) further indicating whether crossing the line is permitted. Standards (mandatory): - "Center line pavement markings, when used, shall be the pavement markings used to delineate the separation of traffic lanes that have opposite directions of travel on a roadway and shall be yellow." - "When used, lane line pavement markings delineating the separation of traffic lanes that have the same direction of travel shall be white." - "The center line markings on two-lane, two-way roadways shall be one of the following as shown in Figure 3B-1: A. Two-direction passing zone markings consisting of a normal width broken yellow line where crossing the center line markings for passing with care is permitted for traffic traveling in either direction; B. One-direction no-passing zone markings consisting of a double yellow line, one of which is a normal width broken yellow line and the other is a normal width solid yellow line, where crossing the center line markings for passing with care is permitted for the traffic traveling adjacent to the broken line, but is prohibited for traffic traveling adjacent to the solid line; or C. Two-direction no-passing zone markings consisting of two normal width solid yellow lines where crossing the center line markings for passing is prohibited for traffic traveling in either direction." - "Except where a reversible lane (see Section 3B.04) or a two-way left-turn lane (see Section 3B.05) is present, the center line markings on undivided two-way roadways with four or more lanes for moving motor vehicle traffic always available shall be the two-direction no-passing zone markings consisting of normal width double solid yellow lines as shown in Figure 3B-2." Options (permitted): - Solid white lane line markings may be used: on approaches to intersections to separate contiguous through lanes; to separate through traffic lanes from auxiliary lanes, such as an added uphill truck lane; and on approaches to crosswalks across multi-lane roadways. - On shared-use paths wide enough for two lanes, a solid yellow center line may be used to separate the two directions of travel where passing or traveling to the left of the line is not permitted, and a broken yellow center line may be used where passing is permitted. Visual evidence: [Image 1] (Figure 3B-2) shows multi-lane, two-way roadways where double solid yellow lines separate the opposing directions (indicated by opposing black arrows) and white lane lines separate same-direction lanes. [Image 2] (Figure 3B-3) shows three-lane, two-way marking where yellow center lines (broken/solid combinations) divide opposing flows and a white broken lane line separates the two same-direction lanes. [Image 3] (Figure 3B-1) shows two-lane, two-way applications with broken and solid yellow center lines dividing opposing traffic, illustrating passing and no-passing zones. [Image 4] and [Image 5] repeat Figures 3B-2 and 3B-3 in the page context, reinforcing the yellow-opposing/white-same-direction distinction. [Image 6] (freeway lane-drop example) shows white lane lines used exclusively between same-direction lanes, with yellow only at the left edge of the directional roadway. [Image 7] shows tubular markers supplementing yellow center line markings between opposing directions and white lane line markings between same-direction lanes at a crosswalk. Citations: - Section 3B.01 Standard §1 (p.540) - Section 3B.06 Standard §1 (p.546) - Section 3B.01 Standard §4 (p.540) - Section 3B.01 Standard §6 (p.540) - Section 3B.06 Option §8 (p.548) - Section 9E.13 Option §1 (p.1106) - Figure 3B-1 (p.540) - Figure 3B-2 (p.541) - Figure 3B-3 (p.542) - Page 582 - Page 583 - Page 595 - Page 674
gold_answer: Yellow center lines separate lanes traveling in opposite directions. White lane lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction.
